2608.24222.title: Measuring Digital Labour Market Transitions with a Digital Semantic Score: An AI-Based Methodology Applied to the Dutch Labour Market
2608.24222.paper_summary: The digital transformation of the Dutch labour market is reshaping occupational language, career pathways, and job-related skills. Addressing these changes requires granular labour market intelligence. This paper develops an AI-based methodology to analyse digitalisation using data covering millions of Dutch job profiles. The methodology combines embedding-based similarity search and large language model classification to map unstructured job information to harmonised ESCO occupations. We also introduce a Digital Semantic Score that measures how strongly job titles and skills are associated with digital concepts relative to a non-digital reference. Using embeddings and cosine similarity to transparent digital and non-digital anchor groups, this indicator moves beyond keyword-based approaches by capturing broader digital meanings in occupational language and worker skill profiles. It enables analysis across occupations, career transitions, emerging job-title vocabulary, and skill digitality. The findings reveal that digitalisation is unevenly distributed across the labour market. Digital job-title language is most prominent among managerial, professional and ICT-related occupations, but is increasingly visible in hybrid business, marketing and automation-related roles. Career-transition analyses show that movement toward digital work is pathway-dependent, while skill analyses highlight the multidimensional nature of digital capability, encompassing technical, hybrid and business-systems skills. By combining profile data, AI-supported occupational classification and semantic scoring, this study advances AI-driven labour market analytics and provides a scalable framework for monitoring digital labour market change. The methodology helps identify emerging skill needs, support reskilling strategies, and inform policies addressing skills mismatches and labour shortages in the Netherlands.
2608.24222.paper_summary_zh: 荷蘭勞動市場的數位轉型正在重塑職業語言、職業道路和與工作相關的技能。應對這些變化需要細緻的勞動市場情報。本文開發了一種基於AI的方法論，利用涵蓋數百萬荷蘭職位的數據來分析數位化。該方法論結合了基於嵌入的相似性搜索和大型語言模型分類，將非結構化的工作信息映射到統一的ESCO職業。我們還引入了一個數位語義分數，衡量工作職稱和技能與數位概念的相關性，相對於非數位參考。通過使用嵌入和餘弦相似度來透明化數位和非數位的錨點群體，這一指標超越了基於關鍵字的方法，捕捉到職業語言和工人技能檔案中更廣泛的數位意義。它使得對職業、職業轉型、新興職稱詞彙和技能數位性進行分析成為可能。研究結果顯示，數位化在勞動市場中的分佈不均。數位職稱語言在管理、專業和ICT相關職業中最為突出，但在混合商業、市場營銷和自動化相關角色中也越來越明顯。職業轉型分析顯示，向數位工作的轉變是依賴於路徑的，而技能分析則突顯了數位能力的多維性，包括技術、混合和商業系統技能。通過結合檔案數據、AI支持的職業分類和語義評分，這項研究推進了基於AI的勞動市場分析，並提供了一個可擴展的框架，用於監測數位勞動市場的變化。該方法論有助於識別新興技能需求，支持再技能策略，並為解決荷蘭的技能不匹配和勞動力短缺問題提供政策建議。
